_comment: Shared test vectors for the ONE operator-SSH-key rule (methodology §5.1,
The rule is setup.ValidOperatorSSHKey in Go. The browser cannot call it, so
ui/lib/enroll.ts carries a mirror — and a mirror nobody executes is how the
three copies that preceded this drifted, each with a comment asking the next
reader to keep them in sync. These vectors are what is actually executed:
api/internal/setup/operatorkeys_test.go runs them against the Go rule and
ui/lib/enroll.test.ts runs the same file against the TypeScript one. A rule
that changes on one side without the other fails a build.
Add a vector when a key shape is decided, not when a test needs padding.
Public keys only — nothing here is a credential.

valid.why: a comment with spaces, which is why the seed line is quoted
valid.key: ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIB3Nzb1c bryce on the blue laptop

valid.why: base64 padding in the key body

invalid.why: empty is handled by the caller, never by the rule

a PEM block pasted where a public key belongs. The marker is spaced out on purpose so this file is not itself something a secret scanner has to be told to ignore; the rule refuses it for the same reason it refuses any first field that is not a known algorithm
a plausible-looking algorithm that is not one
a key body with characters base64 does not use
a double quote, which the seed line cannot carry
two keys on two lines — one key per node, and the rule says so
invalid.key:
ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5 me
ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE6 them

invalid.why: a carriage return from a Windows-saved file
leading whitespace is the caller's to trim, not the rule's to accept
